newsitem.title: USA: Greenbrier says softer demand hurt Q2.
newsitem.headline: Greenbrier says softer demand hurt Q2.

text.p: Greenbrier Cos, reporting lower fiscal second quarter earnings, said Tuesday that softer industry-wide demand for new frieght cars led to lower deliveries for the quarter, affecting manufacturing revenues and profits.
Results for the period were also impacted by stiff competition and a less favorable product mix, it said.
William Furman, president and chief executive officer, said the results were consistent with company expectations.
He said softer demand for railcars will continue to impact results for the balance of the year as the company operates at reduced production levels.
Margins will also be lower due to pricing pressures and product mix, he added.

He said the company is disappointed with the current performance of its logistics business but expects recent cost-cutting efforts and intensified sales efforts to lead to improved results. The improvement will mainly occur in 1998, he said.

On the positive side, the company said its manufacturing backlog of new railcars at February 28 was 1,400 cars valued at $82 million, compared to 1,250 cars valued at $77 million at November 30, 1996.

It said it was pleased with its marine activities as well as the current strength and potential of the segment. It said it had a backlog of three vessels, valued at about $20 million, and had signed a letter of intent to build two barges.
